summary: HTTP broker publisher now implements the outbox transport executor seam with explicit no-gRPC-execution acknowledgement markers.
claim_boundary: This slice wires the existing local HTTP broker-gateway publisher into the existing OutboxTransportExecutor worker injection seam. It executes a real blocking TCP HTTP/1.1 broker publish for a provided OutboxTransportPlan, maps successful broker acknowledgements into OutboxTransportAck, and maps HTTP/config/plan/I/O/status failures into dispatch execution errors for the existing dead-letter path. It explicitly records grpc:not-executed acknowledgement refs and does not claim a gRPC call, SQL mutation, running poller daemon, vendor broker durability, TLS/mTLS, production deployment, delivery SLO, or hyperscaler certification.

source_basis.use: Authoritative HTTP Semantics reference for the POST request and 2xx success-class response boundary used by the local broker-gateway publisher.

facets.F1_simplicity: The existing HttpBrokerPublisher implements the existing OutboxTransportExecutor trait directly; no new crate, framework, async runtime, or third-party dependency is introduced.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The worker injection seam can now exercise a real local broker-gateway publish before later live vendor broker, TLS, service-discovery, and daemon deployment slices make stronger claims.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover local TCP executor success, explicit no-gRPC ack refs, non-2xx HTTP failure mapping, relative AsyncAPI channel handling, absolute URL rejection, unsafe config rejection, invalid channel-path rejection, and payload-budget enforcement.
facets.F4_api_contract: The dispatch app gains a first-class TransportExecutionFailed error, and HttpBrokerPublisher returns the existing OutboxTransportAck shape while preserving event, tenant, audit, policy, and idempotency refs.
facets.F5_quality: Focused adapter/dispatch tests plus the 46-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F6_operations: The executor can be injected into existing worker-cycle code, but it remains a bounded local publish seam; no process supervisor, scheduler, live SQL pool, service discovery, retries, TLS, or production deployment is implemented.
facets.F7_security_privacy: Channel validation rejects absolute URLs, authority-form paths, spaces, controls, CR/LF/NUL header injection, and payload budget overruns; no raw message body, credentials, TLS keys, database URLs, or broker secrets are introduced.
facets.F8_supply_chain: No new external dependency or Cargo.lock change is introduced by this slice; the adapter still depends only on the internal transactional outbox dispatch app.
facets.F9_testing: Focused tests passed for 5 HTTP adapter tests and 6 dispatch app tests; the broad backbone matrix passed 294 unit tests across 46 packages plus one existing ignored metrics adapter doctest.
facets.F10_ci_cd: The touched packages are already included in all four backbone GitHub Actions/Jenkins package matrices from prior slices; this slice does not claim remote CI execution.
facets.F11_observability: Execution success produces OutboxTransportAck fields that can feed worker reports, and execution failure carries transport plus error_ref metadata for dead-letter classification without parsing logs.
facets.F13_reversibility: The bridge is isolated to one trait implementation, one dispatch error variant, one catalog capability update, and task/evidence metadata; reverting restores the prior publisher-only seam without affecting SQL, poller, runtime, or domain crates.
